summary: Olympic summit lookout cab: built 1933 as an L-4, reported abandoned by 1955 and removed or destroyed in 1962; no source describes what remains today.

facts.design: L-4 cab (plan: gabled, shingle roof, heavy shutters, no cupola)
facts.status_note: Removed or destroyed in 1962; the sources differ on which

access.note: Reached by hiking trails from Forest Service roads; a hiking guide calls the peak one of the more popular hiking destinations. Current trail and road conditions not confirmed.

visit.trail_note: Route given as 4 miles one way in a hiking guide; no remains of the lookout are described at the summit

events.note: L-4 cab built (FFLOS, firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb all give 1933)
Panorama photographs taken August 27, 1935 by W.B. Osborne
A USGS party described the cab as abandoned in 1955
FFLOS says removed; firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb say destroyed

evidence.supports: L-4 cab built in 1933 and removed in 1962 (FFLOS)
evidence.quote: Built in 1933, this L-4 cab was removed in 1962.

evidence.supports: L-4 cab built in 1933 on the summit at the lower north end
evidence.quote: Built in 1933, an L-4 cab was located on the summit but at the lower north end.

evidence.supports: L-4 plan: gabled, shingle roof, heavy shutters, no cupola
evidence.quote: L-4 (gabled, shingle roof, heavy shutters, no cupola)

evidence.supports: panorama photographs taken by W.B. Osborne on August 27, 1935
evidence.quote: Panorama photos were taken by W.B. Osborne on August 27, 1935.

evidence.supports: a USGS party described the cab as abandoned in 1955
evidence.quote: A USGS party described it as abandoned in 1955.

evidence.supports: the peak lies in Olympic National Forest
several easy hiking trails to the summit; one of the more popular hiking destinations
evidence.quote: With several easy hiking trails to the top, it is also one of the more popular hiking destinations.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS says the cab was removed in 1962; firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb say destroyed in 1962. None of the sources gives a record or a method, so the story reports both.
FFLOS gives 6,212 ft (1,893 m) for the site, which matches the record. WillhiteWeb's hiking page gives a summit elevation of 6,280 feet. The record keeps the FFLOS value.

notes_for_editor: No staffing names, fires or use after 1955 appear in the sources read, so none are in the story. Access details come from a hiking guide and were not verified against Forest Service sources; check current trail status before publication. The Weebly listing (not cited) gives only the 1935 photos and 'Removed'. The brief record matches FFLOS; no corrections proposed.
